title: Backdoor Cut vs Overplay
description: A wing player reads an overplaying defender and cuts backdoor to the rim instead of fighting for the ball on the perimeter.

content.objective: Recognise an overplaying defender and cut backdoor rather than forcing a pass into denial.
content.setup: A passer at the top faces a wing player being denied by an overplaying defender.
instructions: The defender overplays the passing lane, denying the direct pass.
The wing player reads the overplay and cuts backdoor toward the rim.
The passer delivers a bounce pass or lob over the top timed to the cut.
Reset with the defender varying how hard they overplay.
coachingPoints: Cut the instant the overplay is read — hesitating gives the defender time to recover.
Passer should be ready for the backdoor read, not only the direct pass.
Cut hard and close to the defender's body, not wide around them.
commonMistakes: Standing and fighting for position instead of cutting backdoor.
Passer missing the backdoor cut because they weren't watching for it.
Standing still after a pass instead of moving with purpose.
content.safety: Defender denies with the hands and body only, no grabbing the cutter.
